hints: Look closely at the top of the fork where the parental DNA is still together. The two template strands must be antiparallel, one 5 prime and one 3 prime, and check which side allows continuous growth toward the fork.

Remember DNA polymerase can only add new nucleotides to the 3 prime end, so every new strand must grow 5 prime to 3 prime, and DNA ligase is only needed to join fragments on the discontinuous lagging strand.
walkthrough:
**Check the parental template strands**

Start at the top of the fork where DNA is still double stranded. The two strands must be antiparallel.

Correct pattern is:
$$\text{left template } 5' \text{ (top) to } 3' \text{ (bottom) and right template } 3' \text{ (top) to } 5' \text{ (bottom)}$$

**Apply the 5 prime to 3 prime rule**

DNA polymerase only synthesises in the $5' \to 3'$ direction. That means the growing $3'$ end is always at the polymerase.

On the left, the new strand grows up toward the fork with its $5'$ behind and its $3'$ at the fork. On the right, the new strand grows down away from the fork with its $5'$ at the fork and its $3'$ ahead.

**Identify leading and lagging correctly**

The continuous strand growing toward the fork is the leading strand. The discontinuous strand growing away in fragments is the lagging strand.

Only diagram D has the left side as continuous leading and the right side as fragmented lagging joined by DNA ligase, with all $5'$ and $3'$ ends antiparallel to their templates.

options.A: Parental strands at the top are the wrong way round and the new strands would have to grow 3 prime to 5 prime, which DNA polymerase cannot do.
options.B: Parental polarity is incorrect and the leading and lagging labels are reversed, the ligase is shown on the continuous strand instead of the discontinuous strand.
options.C: Parental top ends are correct but the new strand polarities are reversed and the leading and lagging labels are swapped, so synthesis is shown in the impossible 3 prime to 5 prime direction.
options.D: Shows antiparallel templates, both new strands growing 5 prime to 3 prime, continuous leading strand toward the fork on the left and discontinuous lagging strand with DNA ligase on the right.
